title: Autoscaling on queue depth and on GPU utilisation
design_ref: Autoscaling: scale on the queue the user feels, not on a counter that saturates; cold start is the cost
purpose: Start with one replica at a quiet load, step the load to what four replicas can carry, and let KEDA scale the same Deployment on two different signals (the number of requests waiting plus running, and GPU utilisation); record when each decided, how long the new replicas took to be ready, and the share of requests inside their targets over time.

steps.display: # the settings come from S01's measurements
steps.output:
requests in the system (waiting + running) at the last healthy level of one GPU: 2.3  -> threshold per replica
one GPU's capacity 0.35 req/s -> quiet phase 0.17 req/s (half a replica), step to 1.11 req/s (3.2 replicas)
GPU utilisation counter scale: ratio; target 80% of one GPU per replica

steps.display: kubectl apply -f auto-queue.yaml   # one server behind the router, which re-reads the headless service every 2 s
kubectl apply -f so-auto-queue.yaml   # KEDA ScaledObject, Prometheus trigger, 1 to 4 replicas
steps.output:
query: sum(vllm:num_requests_waiting) + sum(vllm:num_requests_running)
threshold per replica: 2.3

steps.display: kubectl apply -f lg-s10-queue.yaml   # 0.17 req/s for 420 s, then a step to 1.11 req/s for 420 s

steps.output:
rate 0.17: goodput 5.6 tok/s/gpu, attainment 1.00, completed 75/75
rate 1.11: goodput 26.5 tok/s/gpu, attainment 0.82, completed 474/474
done

steps.display: kubectl apply -f auto-util.yaml   # one server behind the router, which re-reads the headless service every 2 s
kubectl apply -f so-auto-util.yaml   # KEDA ScaledObject, Prometheus trigger, 1 to 4 replicas
kubectl apply -f lg-s10-util.yaml   # 0.17 req/s for 420 s, then a step to 1.11 req/s for 420 s

checks.description: both runs completed: the quiet phase and the step were both driven and recorded
checks.because: Each run is one Deployment behind the router with one signal driving KEDA.

checks.description: signal queue: the autoscaler added replicas after the step (more than one replica became Ready)
signal queue: a new replica is not useful at once: it took at least 60 s from creation to Ready
checks.because: Creation to Ready took [125.0, 129.0, 130.0, 132.0] s with the image and weights already on the node's disk; with the model downloaded first it would be longer, and with a new GPU node longer again. This delay, not the decision, is the floor under any scale-up.

checks.description: signal util: the autoscaler added replicas after the step (more than one replica became Ready)
signal util: a new replica is not useful at once: it took at least 60 s from creation to Ready
checks.because: Creation to Ready took [123.0, 124.0, 126.0, 126.0] s with the image and weights already on the node's disk; with the model downloaded first it would be longer, and with a new GPU node longer again. This delay, not the decision, is the floor under any scale-up.

checks.description: at the quiet load (about half of one replica's capacity) the utilisation signal held more replicas than the queue signal did
checks.because: Mean Ready replicas during the quiet phase: 1.0 (queue) against 1.6 (utilisation); Ready when the step arrived: 1 against 2. This check was added after the first run showed the pattern: it is a claim about that run's mechanism, stated here so that a different result would fail it.

notes: Replica-seconds used in the run: queue 1,195, utilisation 1,535. Share of requests inside their targets during the step: queue signal 0.82, utilisation signal 1.00. First decision after the step: queue 19.50591540336609 s, utilisation 51.99502754211426 s. Quiet-phase attainment: queue 1.00, utilisation 1.00.
Not run: scaling the number of GPU nodes (the GPU node group was not allowed to grow beyond the one node that EC2 would give), traffic-based scale from zero, and KServe canary rollouts.
